caseStudies.headline: Scaled Meta spend 6x without breaking ROAS.
caseStudies.detail: Kulture Skin was stuck at ₹3L a month on Meta with a 1.6x ROAS. We rebuilt the account structure, fed it creator-led creative every week and scaled spend to ₹18L a month at 3.4x blended ROAS.
caseStudies.highlights:
Meta spend scaled from ₹3L to ₹18L a month
Blended ROAS doubled from 1.6x to 3.4x
Purchase tracking rebuilt with the Conversions API
180+ creator ads tested in six months
caseStudies.channels: Meta Ads, Instagram Reels, Google Search
caseStudies.services: Meta Ads management, Creative strategy, UGC ad production, Landing page CRO, Tracking & attribution
caseStudies.requirement: Kulture Skin had a loyal organic following and a bestselling vitamin C serum, but paid growth had stalled. The founders came to us with a clear brief: scale Meta Ads past ₹15L a month without ROAS collapsing every time the budget went up, and stop relying on one hero ad that had been running for four months.
caseStudies.goals:
Scale Meta spend from ₹3L to ₹15L+ a month
Hold a blended ROAS of 3x or better while scaling
Build a weekly creative pipeline so no single ad carries the account
Fix purchase tracking so decisions run on real numbers
caseStudies.challenges:
Broken tracking | iOS signal loss and a misfiring pixel meant Meta saw only about 60% of real purchases, so the algorithm was optimising on bad data.
Creative fatigue | One hero video drove 70% of spend. Every time its frequency crossed 3, CPA spiked and the whole account dipped.
Fragmented account | 23 ad sets with overlapping interest audiences were bidding against each other, and none of them left the learning phase.
Scaling crashes | Budget jumps of more than 20% reset learning, and ROAS fell to around 1.2x for days at a time.
caseStudies.approach:
Fix the data first | Set up the Conversions API with server-side events and deduplication, lifting event match quality from 4.1 to 8.7 so Meta could see real buyers again.
Consolidate the account | Collapsed 23 ad sets into one testing campaign and one broad Advantage+ scaling campaign, so budget sat where it learned fastest.
Creative as targeting | Briefed 35 creators on proven angles (texture close-ups, 30-day routines, honest reviews) and tested 20–25 new hooks every week.
Scale on rules, not mood | Ads moved to scaling only after 3 days above target ROAS. Budgets rose 15–20% every 48 hours, with cost caps as guard rails.
caseStudies.execution: The account ran on a weekly loop: creative brief on Monday, new ads live by Thursday, performance review every Monday morning. Losing ads were cut within 72 hours, winners were re-cut into new hooks and formats, and every winning angle got its own landing page section so the click matched the promise.
caseStudies.deliverables:
180+ ad creatives across video, static and carousel
Conversions API and GA4 purchase tracking rebuilt
Two-campaign account structure (testing + Advantage+ scaling)
4 angle-matched landing page variants
Weekly performance report with next week's test plan

caseStudies.resultsSummary: By month three, the account no longer depended on a single ad. By month six, Kulture Skin was spending six times more on Meta at more than double the return, with 14 winning ads in rotation and a creative pipeline that refreshes every week.
caseStudies.quote: Before CLYX, every time we raised the budget we lost money. Now we scale every month and know exactly which ad to put the money behind. The weekly reports alone changed how we run the business.
caseStudies.learnings:
Fix tracking before touching budget | Better signal improved CPA by 18% before a single new ad went live.
Creative is the new targeting | With broad audiences, the hook decided who saw the ad, so creative volume became the main growth lever.
Scale in steps | 15–20% budget increases every 48 hours kept the algorithm stable, where big jumps reset it.

caseStudies.headline: Cut CPA by 42% on Google Search and Shopping.
caseStudies.detail: Nova Nutrition was losing money on Google: rising CPCs, broad match waste and a Performance Max campaign eating brand searches. We rebuilt Search, Shopping and PMax around profit and cut cost per acquisition by 42% in four months.
caseStudies.highlights:
1,400+ negative keywords cut wasted search spend
Brand searches separated from Performance Max
120 product titles rewritten for Shopping
Mobile pages sped up from 5.2s to 1.4s
caseStudies.channels: Google Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube
caseStudies.services: Google Ads management, Product feed optimisation, Performance Max setup, Landing page CRO, Offer testing
caseStudies.requirement: Nova sells whey protein, plant protein and daily supplements. Google was their biggest channel, but cost per acquisition had climbed about 60% over two quarters while revenue stayed flat. They asked us to bring CPA down without cutting volume, and to tell them honestly which campaigns were making money and which were only spending it.
caseStudies.goals:
Cut blended CPA by at least 30%
Stop paying for brand searches through Performance Max
Get Shopping ads showing for high-margin products, not just the cheapest
Lift landing page conversion rate on mobile
caseStudies.challenges:
Broad match waste | 38% of search spend went to irrelevant queries like "protein side effects" and "how to make protein powder at home".
PMax eating brand searches | Performance Max was claiming brand searches people would have made anyway, which made its ROAS look far better than it really was.
Weak product feed | Generic product titles and missing attributes kept Shopping ads out of high-intent searches like "whey isolate 2kg chocolate".
Slow product pages | Mobile product pages took 5.2 seconds to load, and reviews sat four screens below the fold.
caseStudies.approach:
Audit every rupee | Pulled 90 days of search terms, added 1,400+ negative keywords and moved winning queries into exact and phrase match campaigns.
Separate brand from prospecting | Ran brand search on its own small budget and excluded brand terms from PMax, so each campaign was judged on new customers.
Rebuild the feed | Rewrote 120 product titles with flavour, size and protein per serving, and split products into margin tiers with their own ROAS targets.
Fix the landing experience | Built faster mobile product pages with reviews, lab reports and a starter bundle above the fold.
caseStudies.execution: We worked in two-week sprints. The first stopped the waste (negatives and brand separation), the second rebuilt the product feed, and the third and fourth focused on landing pages and offer tests. Every change was measured against profit per order, not just ROAS.
caseStudies.deliverables:
1,400+ negative keywords and a rebuilt keyword structure
120 rewritten product titles and a margin-tiered product feed
Separate brand, Search, Shopping and PMax campaigns
3 mobile landing pages with starter bundles
Profit-per-order reporting dashboard

caseStudies.resultsSummary: Cutting wasted spend and separating brand from prospecting showed the real picture within weeks. Nova now acquires customers for 42% less on the same budget, and bundles raised order values enough to fund YouTube campaigns for new demand.
caseStudies.quote: CLYX was the first agency to show us where our Google money was actually going. Cutting the waste paid for their fee in the first month.
caseStudies.learnings:
Search terms tell the truth | The keyword list looked fine. The search terms report showed a third of the budget going to the wrong people.
Judge PMax without brand | Once brand searches were excluded, PMax ROAS dropped on paper but new-customer growth went up.
The feed is the ad | Better product titles did more for Shopping than any bid change.

caseStudies.headline: ₹1.2Cr in 30 days from one festive sale.
caseStudies.detail: Urban Loom's Diwali sale was always their biggest month, and their most chaotic. We planned it as a six-week performance campaign (warm up, launch, scale, close) and it delivered ₹1.2Cr in revenue at 5.2x ROAS.
caseStudies.highlights:
Six-week festive plan: warm up, launch, scale, close
42,000 WhatsApp sign-ups before the sale opened
Tiered offers kept new-season styles at full price
Stock-synced feed stopped ads on sold-out sizes
caseStudies.channels: Meta Advantage+ Shopping, Catalog ads, Google PMax, WhatsApp
caseStudies.services: Campaign planning, Meta & Google Ads, Catalog ads, Creative production, WhatsApp retargeting
caseStudies.requirement: Urban Loom sells handloom-inspired ethnic wear to young working women. Last year's Diwali sale made ₹38L but ran out of steam after day three, and half the budget went into discounts the brand could not afford. They needed a festive campaign that would cross ₹1Cr in revenue while protecting margin.
caseStudies.goals:
Cross ₹1Cr in festive-month revenue
Keep ROAS above 4x for the whole sale, not just launch day
Grow the WhatsApp list before the sale opened
Avoid deep discounts on new-season styles
caseStudies.challenges:
Sale fatigue | Last year's sale peaked on day one and fell sharply, because the same people saw the same "flat 40% off" ad all month.
Rising festive CPMs | Meta CPMs rise 60–80% in the weeks before Diwali, so cold prospecting during the sale is expensive.
1,800-product catalog | Most products had a single flat-lay image, which made catalog ads look like a spreadsheet.
Stock risk | Bestsellers sold out mid-campaign last year while ads kept sending traffic to out-of-stock pages.
caseStudies.approach:
Warm up before the rush | Started prospecting three weeks early, while CPMs were lower, and sent people to a WhatsApp early-access list instead of a sale page.
Tiered offers, not one discount | Early access got a gift with purchase, the main sale had discounts tiered by cart size, and new-season styles stayed full price.
Make the catalog look good | Added lifestyle frames, price-drop overlays and creator try-on videos so dynamic ads felt like content.
Stock-aware ads | Synced the product feed with inventory every 6 hours, so sold-out sizes dropped out of ads automatically.
caseStudies.execution: The campaign ran in four phases: warm-up (weeks 1–3), early access (2 days), main sale (10 days) and last call (3 days). Each phase had its own creative, audiences and budget. A daily stand-up with the brand's ops team kept ads, stock and offers in sync.
caseStudies.deliverables:
6-week festive media plan with phase budgets
90+ ad creatives, including creator try-on videos
Enhanced catalog with lifestyle frames and price overlays
42,000-person WhatsApp early-access list
Stock-synced product feed for Meta and Google

caseStudies.quote: Last Diwali we were refreshing the dashboard and hoping. This year we had a plan for every single day, and the sale kept growing instead of dying after the first weekend.
caseStudies.learnings:
Win the sale before it starts | The cheapest customers came from the warm-up weeks, before festive CPMs peaked.
Tiered offers protect margin | Cart-size tiers raised order value without discounting the whole catalog.
Ops is part of performance | Syncing stock with the feed saved budget that would have gone to sold-out products.

caseStudies.headline: Cost per enrolment down 61% with a webinar funnel.
caseStudies.detail: SkillSprint was buying leads that never picked up the phone. We replaced instant-form lead ads with a free live masterclass funnel, qualified leads before sales called them, and cut the cost of a paid enrolment by 61%.
caseStudies.highlights:
Instant forms replaced with a live masterclass funnel
Every lead scored before sales picked up the phone
CRM outcomes sent back to Meta to train bidding
First call in 12 minutes instead of 26 hours
caseStudies.channels: Meta Lead Ads, YouTube, Google Search, WhatsApp
caseStudies.services: Funnel strategy, Meta & YouTube Ads, Landing pages, Lead scoring, CRM & WhatsApp automation
caseStudies.requirement: SkillSprint runs a 16-week data analytics course priced at ₹45,000. Their Meta lead ads brought in cheap leads at ₹90 each, but fewer than 1% enrolled, and the sales team was burning out calling people who did not remember filling in the form. They asked us to lower the cost of an actual enrolment, not the cost of a lead.
caseStudies.goals:
Cut cost per paid enrolment by at least 40%
Raise lead-to-enrolment rate above 3%
Give the sales team fewer, better leads
Track every enrolment back to the ad that started it
caseStudies.challenges:
Cheap leads, no buyers | Instant forms made sign-up effortless, so many leads were students and job seekers who could not afford the course.
No link from ad to sale | Enrolments closed on the phone, so Meta never learned which leads became paying students.
Slow follow-up | Leads waited 26 hours on average for a first call, by which time interest had faded.
Long decision cycle | A ₹45,000 course takes 2–3 weeks to decide on, but ads were judged on 7-day results.
caseStudies.approach:
Sell the masterclass, not the course | Ads offered a free 90-minute live masterclass on analytics careers, so people showed real intent by giving up an evening.
Qualify on the landing page | A short form asked about experience, salary band and start date, and scored every lead before it reached sales.
Send sales data back to Meta | Connected the CRM through the Conversions API, so "attended", "qualified" and "enrolled" events trained the algorithm on buyers.
Follow up within minutes | WhatsApp reminders before each masterclass, and a sales call assigned within 15 minutes of attending.
caseStudies.execution: Two masterclasses ran every week. Ads drove registrations, WhatsApp handled reminders, and sales only called people who attended and scored as qualified. Every Friday we reviewed cost per attendee, attendance rate and enrolments by ad, and moved budget accordingly.
caseStudies.deliverables:
Masterclass funnel: landing page, registration flow and thank-you page
Lead scoring model inside the CRM
Offline conversions sent to Meta and Google
WhatsApp reminder and nurture sequences
60+ video ads, including faculty and alumni stories

caseStudies.resultsSummary: Leads became more expensive, and that was the point. Each lead now costs ₹185 instead of ₹90, but five times more of them enrol, so the cost of a paying student fell by 61% and monthly enrolments more than doubled on the same budget.
caseStudies.quote: We stopped judging marketing on cost per lead. Our sales team now talks to people who actually showed up and want to learn, and our enrolments have more than doubled.
caseStudies.learnings:
Optimise for the sale, not the lead | Cheaper leads looked good in Ads Manager and bad in the bank account.
Friction filters | Asking people to attend a live session removed low-intent leads before sales spent time on them.
Speed wins deals | Calling within 15 minutes of the masterclass made the biggest single difference to enrolments.

caseStudies.headline: 3,200 qualified leads for a new project launch.
caseStudies.detail: Aranya Homes needed site visits for a new 2 and 3 BHK project in Pune. We ran Google Search, Meta and YouTube into one tightly qualified funnel and delivered 3,200 qualified leads at 55% lower cost per lead than their previous launch.
caseStudies.highlights:
Locality and commute keywords instead of city-wide terms
Budget, timeline and loan questions in every lead form
Drone and walkthrough videos answered questions early
41 units sold in the launch window
caseStudies.channels: Google Search, Meta Lead Ads, YouTube, WhatsApp
caseStudies.services: Launch media plan, Google & Meta Ads, Lead qualification, Landing pages, Sales reporting
caseStudies.requirement: Aranya was launching a 240-unit project in Pune. Their previous launch, run through property portals and brokers, cost ₹2,900 per lead, and the sales team said most leads were "just browsing". They wanted leads who could afford an ₹85L–1.4Cr home, and site visits booked every weekend.
caseStudies.goals:
Generate 3,000+ qualified leads in four months
Keep cost per qualified lead under ₹2,500
Book 60+ site visits a month
Reach NRI buyers in the Gulf and the US
caseStudies.challenges:
Junk leads | Earlier lead ads brought in renters, brokers and people with budgets far below the project price.
Expensive keywords | Searches like "2 BHK in Pune" cost ₹60–90 per click and were shared with every developer in the city.
Long buying cycle | Home buyers take 3–6 months to decide, so leads had to be nurtured, not just collected.
No feedback loop | Sales tracked lead status in spreadsheets, so the ad platforms never knew which leads were real.
caseStudies.approach:
Target micro-markets | Built search campaigns around specific localities, commute routes and IT parks near the project instead of generic city keywords.
Qualify inside the form | Lead forms asked about budget, timeline and home loan status, adding a step on purpose to filter out casual browsers.
Walkthrough-first creative | Used drone footage, sample flat walkthroughs and price-per-sq-ft breakdowns, so the ad answered questions before the call.
Close the loop | Moved sales onto a simple CRM and sent "qualified" and "site visit" events back to Google and Meta every day.
caseStudies.execution: Campaigns went live three weeks before the sales office opened, building a waitlist for launch pricing. After launch, weekday ads drove enquiries and weekend ads pushed site visit bookings. Our team joined the developer's sales review every Monday to match ad data with feedback from the ground.
caseStudies.deliverables:
Locality-led Google Search structure with 40 ad groups
Launch landing page with floor plans and an EMI calculator
Drone and walkthrough video ads for Meta and YouTube
NRI campaigns for the UAE, Saudi Arabia and the US
Daily CRM sync with offline conversions

caseStudies.quote: For the first time, our sales team asked marketing for more leads instead of complaining about them. Weekend site visits have been full since the second month.
caseStudies.learnings:
Quality is a targeting setting | Once the platforms received qualified-lead data, cost per qualified lead fell month on month.
Local beats generic | Locality and commute keywords converted at twice the rate of "flats in Pune".
Show the home before the call | Walkthrough videos produced leads who already knew the price and layout.

caseStudies.headline: Nearly 2x paying subscribers on the same budget.
caseStudies.detail: FitPulse had plenty of installs but few paying subscribers. We moved app campaigns from install bidding to trial and subscription events, rebuilt creative around real workouts, and cut the cost of a paying subscriber by 48%.
caseStudies.highlights:
Bidding moved from installs to trials and subscriptions
Subscription tracking fixed on Android and iOS
120+ real workout videos replaced stock footage
Install-to-paid rate up from 1.5% to 3.4%
caseStudies.channels: Google App Campaigns, Meta App Ads, Apple Search Ads
caseStudies.services: App campaign strategy, MMP & event setup, Creative production, App store optimisation, Retention ads
caseStudies.requirement: FitPulse offers home and gym workout plans on a ₹299 monthly subscription. Their campaigns delivered installs at ₹28 each, but only 1.5% of people who installed ever paid. The founders wanted growth in paying subscribers, with clear data on which campaigns brought in people who stayed.
caseStudies.goals:
Cut cost per paying subscriber by 35% or more
Optimise campaigns for trials and subscriptions, not installs
Improve day-30 retention of paid users
Lift app store conversion rate
caseStudies.challenges:
Optimising for the wrong event | Campaigns bid for installs, so the platforms found people who install apps but never pay.
Messy event tracking | The MMP and Firebase reported different numbers, and the subscription event did not fire on iOS at all.
Generic creative | Stock-style gym footage looked like every other fitness app, with a hook rate under 15%.
Weak store listing | Screenshots showed features instead of results, and the store page converted only 21% of visitors.
caseStudies.approach:
Fix the events | Rebuilt tracking in the MMP and Firebase so trial start and paid subscription fired reliably on Android and iOS.
Bid for value | Moved Google App Campaigns to target CPA on trial start, then to subscription once volume allowed. Meta followed the same path.
Real workouts, real people | Filmed 10-minute home workouts with trainers and members, cut into 15-second "try this" hooks.
Optimise the store page | Tested new screenshots, a preview video and results-led copy on the Play Store and App Store.
caseStudies.execution: We ran fortnightly creative sprints of 15–20 new videos, with a weekly look at cohort data: cost per trial, trial-to-paid rate and day-30 retention by campaign. Budget only moved towards campaigns whose subscribers were still active after 30 days.
caseStudies.deliverables:
MMP and Firebase event setup for trial and subscription
Google App, Meta and Apple Search Ads campaigns rebuilt
120+ workout-led video ads
New store screenshots and preview video
Cohort dashboard with day-30 retention by campaign

caseStudies.resultsSummary: Installs got slightly more expensive, but the people installing were far more likely to pay. FitPulse now adds almost twice as many paying subscribers each month on the same budget, and more of them are still working out after 30 days.
caseStudies.quote: We used to celebrate cheap installs. CLYX made us look at who actually pays and stays, and our subscriber growth has nearly doubled since.
caseStudies.learnings:
Bid for the event you are paid on | Moving from install to trial to subscription bidding changed who the algorithm found.
Show the product working | Real workout clips beat polished brand videos on hook rate and on trial starts.
The store page is a landing page | Store listing tests lifted conversion on every channel at once.
